RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Morgan Grant
Member ID: W585722922
Reference Number: POC-8EE886247D-14307
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-07
Requested Service: Partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement, CPT 27446
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-03

To the Aetna Appeals Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (partial knee replacement), dated 2026-08-07, on the stated basis that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." This appeal is submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in the denial notice. My treating surgeon is Dr. Okafor, orthopedic surgery.

I understand Aetna's medical-necessity criteria for this procedure are set out in Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty" (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html). I have not been able to independently confirm the effective/last-revised date of the version of CPB 0660 that was applied to my request, and I am relying below only on language I have directly retrieved from the publicly posted policy text. If a different version or date applies to my determination, I request that Aetna identify it and provide me a copy.

CPB 0660 states that unicompartmental knee arthroplasty "is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria." Below I address each criterion using the plan's own quoted language and the documentation in my chart.

1. "Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint"
   This is met. I have had 9 months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest. I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake 3-4 times nightly due to pain, both documented in my chart.

2. "Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination"
   This is met in part. My exam documents range of motion limited by pain and positive provocative testing on the affected side. [Specific documentation of crepitus and/or effusion, if not already recorded, to be confirmed by Dr. Okafor's office.]

3. "Member must have intact, stable ligaments, in particular the anterior cruciate ligament"
   [Ligament stability/ACL exam findings are not included in the clinical summary provided to me; a supplemental note from Dr. Okafor confirming ligament stability should be submitted with this appeal.]

4. "Patient's knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) is not limited to 90 degrees or less"
   [Specific range-of-motion measurement in degrees is not included in the clinical summary provided to me; a supplemental note from Dr. Okafor documenting the exact arc of motion should be submitted with this appeal.]

5. "Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) ... affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint"
   This is met. MRI dated 2026-07-06 documents "full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition" and Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 changes limited to the medial compartment.

6. "History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record ... with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy"
   My record documents 8 weeks (16 visits) of supervised, in-person physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion (2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07), 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection (2026-05-25) that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. I acknowledge that 8 weeks of formal physical therapy is less than the 12-week baseline referenced in the policy. However, the same policy provides that "[c]onservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral)." My MRI documents exactly this finding — bone-on-bone apposition in the medial (weight-bearing) compartment — and I ask that this exception be applied to my case. I am asking Dr. Okafor to submit an addendum "clearly document[ing] why such [further conservative] approach is not reasonable," as the policy requires when this exception is invoked. [Addendum from Dr. Okafor documenting rationale to be submitted with this appeal.]
   I further note that the conservative measures I did complete satisfy the specific modalities the policy lists — "Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics" (6 months of NSAIDs), "Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises" and "Supervised physical therapy" (16 supervised PT visits), and "Therapeutic injections into the knee" (corticosteroid injection 2026-05-25). [Documentation of "activity modification," and of assistive device use if applicable, to be confirmed and submitted if not already in the record.]

7. Absolute contraindications
   The policy lists several absolute contraindications to joint replacement, including "Corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty." My corticosteroid injection was administered 2026-05-25. I ask that surgery be scheduled, and request that Aetna confirm, for a date at least 12 weeks after 2026-05-25 (i.e., on or after approximately 2026-08-17) so that this contraindication does not apply. [Planned surgical date to be confirmed by Dr. Okafor's office and provided to Aetna.] I have no active joint or systemic infection, no active skin infection or open wound at the surgical site, no known vascular insufficiency, muscular atrophy, or neuromuscular disease affecting the leg, no osseous abnormality precluding implant support, and no known allergy to implant components, based on my current clinical evaluation. [Confirmation of the absence of each of these specific findings should be documented by Dr. Okafor's office if not already in the chart.]

8. Contraindications specific to unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
   The policy lists specific contraindications including "Previous proximal tibial osteotomy or distal femoral osteotomy," "Tibial or femoral shaft deformity," "Radiographic evidence of medial or lateral subluxation," "Flexion contracture greater than 15 degrees," "Varus deformity greater than 15 degrees (medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty)," "Inflammatory or crystalline arthropathy," and "Subchondral bone loss due to large subchondral cysts or extensive focal osteonecrosis." None of these are noted in the clinical summary provided to me. [Specific measurements/findings on these items — prior osteotomy history, deformity/subluxation measurements, and absence of inflammatory/crystalline arthropathy or extensive osteonecrosis — should be confirmed and documented by Dr. Okafor's office and submitted with this appeal.]

9. Diabetes-related criterion
   The policy states, "If member is diabetic, their hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to knee arthroplasty." [If I am diabetic, a current HbA1c result should be submitted with this appeal; if I am not diabetic, this criterion does not apply.]

10. BMI/age relative contraindication
   The policy identifies relative contraindications of "morbid obesity (BMI greater than 40), age less than 50 years," in which case "[m]embers with relative contraindications should exhaust all nonsurgical treatment options." My BMI is 29, which is below the morbid-obesity threshold identified in the policy, so this relative contraindication and its associated requirement to exhaust all nonsurgical options before considering the 12-week floor insufficient does not appear to apply to me. [Age to be confirmed in the record.]

Summary
Based on the criteria quoted directly from CPB 0660 and the documentation summarized above, I believe the medical necessity standard for unicompartmental knee arthroplasty is met or can be met with the limited supplemental documentation identified above (ligament stability, exact range-of-motion measurement, deformity/subluxation measurements, planned surgical date relative to the corticosteroid injection, and HbA1c if applicable). I am requesting that Dr. Okafor's office submit these supplemental items promptly in support of this appeal.

I respectfully request that Aetna reverse the denial of CPT 27446 and approve prior authorization for this procedure. I also request a peer-to-peer review between Dr. Okafor and Aetna's medical reviewer, and a copy of the complete file, including the specific version of CPB 0660 and any internal criteria, guidelines, or clinical rationale relied upon in the original denial, as I am entitled to receive under applicable appeal rights.

Enclosed / to follow under separate cover:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07, 16 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-25)
- MRI report dated 2026-07-06
- Clinic notes documenting functional limitations and physical examination findings
- [Supplemental addendum from Dr. Okafor addressing items identified above]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and notify me and Dr. Okafor's office of the outcome and of any further information needed.

Sincerely,

Morgan Grant
